title: Running ComfyUI safely on a network
hook: ComfyUI has no login. What --listen, CORS, TLS and --multi-user each really do, tested against the real middleware.

verified.claim: The threat model and the quotes.
The status table: the real middleware functions, extracted with ast, on mocked aiohttp requests. The lab's port gives the same answers.
Turning on CORS installs its middleware instead of the origin check.
--listen with no value means 0.0.0.0,:: and main.py splits on the comma.
TLS needs both files, and verify_mode is CERT_NONE.
The open routes in the table.
Partner tokens are removed from what is stored.
SaveImage refuses a path outside the output folder.
Simple POST requests need no preflight.
verified.ref: MDN CORS guide, fetched from its repository 2026-11-01

verified.claim: GET /queue returns extra_data with the client id, and a socket that reuses a clientId replaces the old one.

unchecked: We did not attack a running server. The table comes from the middleware functions alone, with mocked requests, and the browser rows assume what a browser would send.
Browsers keep adding rules of their own for pages that call private addresses. We did not test any.
We did not read the Manager, agent, deploy-to-cloud or assets routes in depth. They add more surface.
The proxy advice is general. We did not test a proxy, including websocket passing.
The lab's port only knows localhost and addresses as loopback, while the real is_loopback also looks up names.
